premises.statement: For every candidate with a LinkedIn URL, the social-media row selected as highest-index across all platforms is a LinkedIn row.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY candidate_id ORDER BY "index" DESC) AS row_num ... FROM staging.stg_greenhouse__social_media_address; ... WHERE is_linkedin AND row_num = 1
premises.alternative: The contract requires ranking within LinkedIn entries: "from social media URLs containing 'linkedin' ignoring case, choose the row with the highest social_media_index per candidate".
premises.reason: A higher-index entry for another platform would suppress an otherwise available LinkedIn URL.

premises.statement: For every candidate with a GitHub URL, the social-media row selected as highest-index across all platforms is a GitHub row.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: social_ranked AS (... ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY candidate_id ORDER BY "index" DESC) AS row_num ...); ... WHERE is_github AND row_num = 1
premises.alternative: The contract requires ranking within GitHub entries: "from social media URLs containing 'github' ignoring case, choose the row with the highest social_media_index per candidate".
premises.reason: A higher-index entry for another platform would suppress an otherwise available GitHub URL.

premises.statement: Each application_id has at most one matching row in staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: LEFT JOIN staging.stg_greenhouse__job_application AS ja ON au.application_id = ja.application_id
premises.alternative: The junction table declares the composite primary key "[job_id, application_id]", which permits multiple jobs per application, while application_info requires "One row per application_id".
premises.reason: Multiple job associations would multiply application rows and violate the required output grain.

premises.statement: Every candidate group surviving the candidate-tag joins has at least one non-null tag name.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: BOOL_OR(LOWER(t.name) LIKE '%technical%') AS has_technical_tag, BOOL_OR(LOWER(t.name) LIKE '%experience%') AS has_experience_tag
premises.alternative: The contract explicitly allows groups with no non-null names and requires both flags to be "otherwise FALSE; never NULL".
premises.reason: An all-null-name group would produce null flags without an explicit false default.
